sections.title: Tycker, tror and personal viewpoints: meaning and form
body: Goal: State preferences and opinions, and separate what you think from what you believe is true.
Core vocabulary: en åsikt, bekväm, verka. Key phrases: Jag tycker om området. · Jag tycker att bussen är bekväm. · Jag tror att tåget är försenat.

Tycka om means to like something. Tycka att introduces an opinion or evaluation. Tro att introduces a belief, prediction or uncertain fact. Ask Vad tycker du om …? for an evaluation and Tror du att …? for a belief.
Say the examples aloud, notice the pattern, and then change one detail rather than memorising a fixed script.

examples.en: I think the bus is comfortable.

examples.en: I believe the train is delayed.

sections.title: Register, evidence and independent use
body: Register model: “Vad tycker du om förslaget?” is a neutral discussion way to express “What is your view?”.
For listening and reading, answer from a specific word or phrase. For speaking and writing, make the recipient, purpose and next action clear.
Attempt the task before using the model. Improve one high-impact feature, then perform it again with the transfer condition.

assignment.title: Four-skill task and transfer
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: First listen without a transcript. Answer: What is the speaker's opinion of the task? Replay once and identify the exact words that prove the answer.

READ: Read for purpose and evidence. Answer: What does Chen believe? Mark the shortest phrase that supports your choice.

SPEAK: Compare two ways to travel. Say what you like, give one evaluation and add one belief that you are not certain about. Make a first attempt, check clarity and repeat once.

WRITE: Answer a neighbourhood survey in 70–90 words. Give one positive opinion, one criticism and one suggestion. Check reader, purpose, required details and next action.

TRANSFER: The survey is now about a public library rather than your neighbourhood; adapt your viewpoint and reasons.

BETWEEN LESSON · Optional, 5 minutes: retrieve the three key phrases without looking, then use one in a new sentence.
